title: Quantitatively Measuring and Contrastively Exploring Heterogeneity for Domain Generalization

problem.claim: Domain generalization aims to train models that generalize to unseen target domains using several source domains.

gap.claim: Original domain labels may be suboptimal supervision because they may lack domain heterogeneity, and existing re-dividing methods lack a metric for selecting the most heterogeneous pattern.

contributions.claim: The paper characterizes domain heterogeneity as mainly residing in variant features under an invariant learning framework.
It proposes a learning potential-guided contrastive metric for domain heterogeneity by promoting learning of variant features.

It proposes Heterogeneity-based Two-stage Contrastive Learning (HTCL), which generates a heterogeneous domain-dividing pattern and then applies invariance-aimed contrastive learning using domain- and class-informed stable relations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe HTCL as a novel method for domain generalization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show HTCL better captures domain heterogeneity and achieves strong generalization performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames domain generalization as learning from source domains for performance on unseen target domains.
It argues that original domain labels may be noisy or insufficiently heterogeneous, while existing domain re-division methods lack a heterogeneity metric.
It defines heterogeneity through variant features and introduces a contrastive metric guided by learning potential.
It introduces HTCL with a heterogeneity-seeking first stage and an invariance-aimed second stage based on reconstructed domain- and class-informed pairs.
The authors report improved heterogeneity discovery and generalization performance in extensive experiments.

source_observation.claim: Labels that identify domains may not provide the most useful supervision when they do not reflect meaningful heterogeneity.

interpretation.claim: Supervision quality can depend on whether labels expose the variation relevant to the learning objective.

application.claim: For multi-domain learning, evaluate or construct domain partitions using an explicit heterogeneity measure before using them for generalization training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that re-partitioning or heterogeneity-based supervision is beneficial for tasks beyond the reported domain-generalization setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, quantitative gains, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not provide the formal definition or implementation details of the heterogeneity metric.
The abstract does not report computational costs, limitations, or failure cases.
